name: What should homeowners ask before signing a custom spa contract?

mainEntity.name: What should homeowners ask before signing a custom spa contract?
mainEntity.text: What should homeowners ask before signing a custom spa contract?

acceptedAnswer.text: Before signing a contract, homeowners should make sure the builder has clearly defined the full scope of work. That includes excavation, structural work, plumbing, electrical, finishes, equipment, startup, permits, inspections, and any hardscape restoration. The contract should also state what is excluded, how change orders are handled, when payments are due, and what warranty coverage applies to workmanship and equipment. It is equally important to ask who will manage the permit process and how the contractor handles unforeseen site conditions such as bad soil, drainage problems, or utility conflicts. In the Los Angeles area, where lots and permit requirements vary by city, clarity is essential. A strong contract reduces surprises by making assumptions visible before construction begins. Homeowners should never rely on a verbal summary alone if the spa is a significant investment. The contract should read like a roadmap for the actual job.
acceptedAnswer.description: Before signing, homeowners should ask about scope, permits, timeline, equipment, exclusions, payment schedule, change orders, warranty, and who handles inspections. Clear answers to those items reduce the chance of budget overruns and construction delays.
